snippet.title: Discover the bold beauty of Mursi lip plates link between identity & tradition #culture #traditional
snippet.description:
Beauty or pain? For Mursi women, lip plates are more than decoration—they’re culture, status, and survival.

In the Omo Valley of Ethiopia, the Mursi tribe carries one of the world’s most striking traditions: the lip plate. Worn mostly by women, these large clay or wooden discs are inserted into the lower lip, symbolizing beauty, strength, and social status. But this is more than just body modification—it’s a cultural statement passed down for centuries. Some say the larger the plate, the greater the respect. Others see it as a way of resisting colonial influence and preserving identity. Pain, pride, and heritage come together in this powerful ritual. Would you endure this for beauty?
